subject: Maths
explanation:
To evaluate $f(x) = \int \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{x^{2/3}+2x^{1/2}}$, substitute $x = t^6$, so $\mathrm{d}x = 6t^5 \mathrm{d}t$:
$$f(x) = \int \frac{6t^5}{t^4 + 2t^3} \mathrm{d}t = \int \frac{6t^2}{t+2} \mathrm{d}t = 6 \int \left(t - 2 + \frac{4}{t+2}\right) \mathrm{d}t$$
$$= 6\left(\frac{t^2}{2} - 2t + 4\ln|t+2|\right) + C = 3t^2 - 12t + 24\ln|t+2| + C$$
Substituting back $t = x^{1/6}$:
$$f(x) = 3x^{1/3} - 12x^{1/6} + 24\ln(x^{1/6}+2) + C$$
Given $f(0) = 24\ln(2) + C = -26 + 24\ln(2) \implies C = -26$.
Now for $x = 1$:
$$f(1) = 3(1) - 12(1) + 24\ln(3) - 26 = -35 + 24\ln(3)$$
Thus, $\mathrm{a} = -35$ and $\mathrm{b} = 24$.
$$\mathrm{a} + \mathrm{b} = -35 + 24 = -11$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Given vectors $\overrightarrow{AB} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.
Lengths: $|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{9+1+1} = \sqrt{11}$ and $|\overrightarrow{AC}| = \sqrt{1+1+9} = \sqrt{11}$.
The angle $\theta$ between $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ satisfies:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}}{|\overrightarrow{AB}||\overrightarrow{AC}|} = \frac{3(1) + 1(-1) + (-1)(3)}{11} = -\frac{1}{11}$$
Since point $P$ is equidistant from lines $AB$ and $AC$ in their plane, $\overrightarrow{AP}$ lies along the angle bisector of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$.
For the internal angle bisector, the angle between $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AP}$ is $\frac{\theta}{2}$:
$$\cos\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{11} \implies \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\frac{6}{11}}$$
Area of $\triangle ABP = \frac{1}{2} |\overrightarrow{AB}| |\overrightarrow{AP}| \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{11} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{6}{11}} = \frac{\sqrt{30}}{4}$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Expected value is:
$$\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{X}) = \sum x_i P(x_i) = \frac{\mathrm{k}}{15}\left[4(2) + \frac{30}{7}(1) + \frac{32}{7}(2) + \frac{34}{7}(3) + \frac{36}{7}(1) + \frac{38}{7}(2) + \frac{40}{7}(3) + 6(1)\right]$$
$$= \frac{\mathrm{k}}{15}\left[14 + \frac{30+64+102+36+76+120}{7}\right] = \frac{\mathrm{k}}{15}\left[14 + \frac{428}{7}\right] = \frac{\mathrm{k}}{15}\left[\frac{526}{7}\right]$$
Given $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{X}) = \frac{263}{15} \implies \frac{526\mathrm{k}}{105} = \frac{263}{15} \implies \mathrm{k} = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5$.
Evaluating the outcomes for $\mathrm{X}$:
$$\mathrm{X} \in \{14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21\}$$
We need $P(\mathrm{X} < 20) = 1 - P(\mathrm{X} = 20) - P(\mathrm{X} = 21)$:
$$P(\mathrm{X} < 20) = 1 - \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{15} = 1 - \frac{4}{15} = \frac{11}{15}$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Intersection of $P_1: y = 4x^2$ and $P_2: y = x^2 + 27$:
$$4x^2 = x^2 + 27 \implies 3x^2 = 27 \implies x = \pm 3$$
Area between $P_1$ and $P_2$:
$$A_1 = \int_{-3}^3 (27 - 3x^2)\,\mathrm{d}x = 2\left[27(3) - 3^3\right] = 108$$
Intersection of $y = \alpha x$ and $P_1: y = 4x^2$ occurs at $x = 0$ and $x = \frac{\alpha}{4}$.
Area between line and $P_1$:
$$A_2 = \int_0^{\alpha/4} (\alpha x - 4x^2)\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[\frac{\alpha x^2}{2} - \frac{4x^3}{3}\right]_0^{\alpha/4} = \frac{\alpha^3}{32} - \frac{\alpha^3}{48} = \frac{\alpha^3}{96}$$
Given $A_1 = 6 A_2$:
$$108 = 6 \left(\frac{\alpha^3}{96}\right) = \frac{\alpha^3}{16} \implies \alpha^3 = 1728 \implies \alpha = 12$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Rewriting the differential equation in standard linear form:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - \frac{1}{x}y = x\cot x$$
Integrating factor $\mathrm{I.F.} = \mathrm{e}^{-\int \frac{1}{x}\mathrm{d}x} = \frac{1}{x}$.
Multiplying and integrating:
$$\frac{y}{x} = \int \cot x\,\mathrm{d}x = \ln|\sin x| + C \implies y(x) = x\ln(\sin x) + Cx$$
Given $y\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{2}\ln(1) + C\frac{\pi}{2} \implies C = 1$.
Thus, $y(x) = x\ln(\sin x) + x$.
Now:
$$y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}\ln(1/2) + \frac{\pi}{6} = -\frac{\pi}{6}\ln 2 + \frac{\pi}{6} \implies 6y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\pi\ln 2 + \pi$$
$$y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4}\ln(1/\sqrt{2}) + \frac{\pi}{4} = -\frac{\pi}{8}\ln 2 + \frac{\pi}{4} \implies 8y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\pi\ln 2 + 2\pi$$
Subtracting gives:
$$6y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) - 8y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = (-\pi\ln 2 + \pi) - (-\pi\ln 2 + 2\pi) = -\pi$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
General point on line $L_1$: $M(1+\lambda, 2\lambda, 1+\lambda)$.
For foot of perpendicular from $P(3, 2, 1)$:
$$\overrightarrow{PM} = (\lambda-2, 2\lambda-2, \lambda)$$
$$\overrightarrow{PM}\cdot (1, 2, 1) = 0 \implies (\lambda-2) + 2(2\lambda-2) + \lambda = 0 \implies 6\lambda = 6 \implies \lambda = 1$$
Foot of perpendicular is $M(2, 2, 2)$.
Image point $Q = 2M - P = (1, 2, 3)$.
Distance from $Q(1, 2, 3)$ to line $L_2: \frac{x-9}{3} = \frac{y-9}{2} = \frac{z-5}{-2} = \mu$:
A point on line $L_2$ is $A(9, 9, 5)$ and direction vector is $\vec{v} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.
$$\overrightarrow{QA} = 8\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$$
$$\overrightarrow{QA} \times \vec{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 8 & 7 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-14 - 4) - \hat{j}(-16 - 6) + \hat{k}(16 - 21) = -18\hat{i} + 22\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$$
Magnitude $|\overrightarrow{QA} \times \vec{v}| = \sqrt{(-18)^2 + 22^2 + (-5)^2} = \sqrt{324 + 484 + 25} = \sqrt{833} = 7\sqrt{17}$.
$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{9 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{17}$.
Distance $d = \frac{|\overrightarrow{QA} \times \vec{v}|}{|\vec{v}|} = \frac{7\sqrt{17}}{\sqrt{17}} = 7$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
For the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{144} + \frac{y^2}{169} = 1$, $b^2 = 169 > a^2 = 144$, so foci lie on the y-axis:
$$b^2 e_E^2 = b^2 - a^2 = 169 - 144 = 25 \implies b e_E = 5 \implies \text{foci are } (0, \pm 5)$$
For the hyperbola $\frac{y^2}{\lambda^2} - \frac{x^2}{16} = 1$, the foci are $(0, \pm 5)$:
$$b_H^2 e_H^2 = b_H^2 + a_H^2 = \lambda^2 + 16 = 25 \implies \lambda^2 = 9 \implies \lambda = 3$$
Eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{a_H^2}{b_H^2}} = \sqrt{1 + \frac{16}{9}} = \frac{5}{3}$.
Length of latus rectum $L = \frac{2 a_H^2}{b_H} = \frac{2(16)}{3} = \frac{32}{3}$.
$$24(e + L) = 24\left(\frac{5}{3} + \frac{32}{3}\right) = 24\left(\frac{37}{3}\right) = 296$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Statement I: $f(x) = \frac{x}{1+|x|}$.
For $x \ge 0$, $f'(x) = \frac{1}{(1+x)^2} > 0$; for $x < 0$, $f'(x) = \frac{1}{(1-x)^2} > 0$.
$f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbf{R}$, so it is one-one. Statement I is True.

Statement II: $f(x) = \frac{x^2+4x-30}{x^2-8x+18}$.
Since $x^2-8x+18 = (x-4)^2 + 2 > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}$, $f(x)$ is continuous everywhere.
As $x \to \infty$, $f(x) \to 1$ and as $x \to -\infty$, $f(x) \to 1$. By Rolle's theorem/IVT, $f(x)$ attains values more than once, so it is many-one. Statement II is True.
Thus, both Statement I and Statement II are true.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Center is $C(1, -2)$, one focus is $S(3, -2)$, and one vertex is $V(5, -2)$.
Since the y-coordinates are equal, the major axis is parallel to the x-axis.
Semi-major axis $a = |5 - 1| = 4$.
Distance from center to focus $ae = |3 - 1| = 2$.
$$b^2 = a^2 - (ae)^2 = 16 - 4 = 12$$
Length of latus rectum $= \frac{2b^2}{a} = \frac{2(12)}{4} = 6$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
As $\theta \to 0$, $x^{2/\theta} \to \infty$ for $|x| > 1$, and $x^{2/\theta} \to 0$ for $|x| < 1$.
Thus:
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} -\frac{\sin(x-1)}{x-1}, & |x| > 1 \\ \cos\pi x, & |x| < 1 \end{cases}$$
At $x = 1$, $x^{2/\theta} = 1$, so $f(1) = \frac{\cos\pi - 0}{1 + 0} = -1$.
$$\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} -\frac{\sin(x-1)}{x-1} = -1, \quad \lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \cos\pi = -1$$
Since $\lim_{x\to 1} f(x) = f(1) = -1$, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 1$. Statement (I) is False.

At $x = -1$, $f(-1) = 1 - \sin 2$, but $\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x) = -\frac{\sin 2}{2} \ne \lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x) = -1$, so $f(x)$ is discontinuous at $x = -1$. Statement (II) is False.
Therefore, neither (I) nor (II) is True.

subject: Maths
explanation:
The given sum is a GP with first term $(1+x)^{1000}$, ratio $\frac{x}{1+x}$, and 1001 terms:
$$S = (1+x)^{1000} \frac{1 - \left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^{1001}}{1 - \frac{x}{1+x}} = (1+x)^{1001} - x^{1001}$$
Coefficient of $x^{499}$ is $\binom{1001}{499}$ and coefficient of $x^{500}$ is $\binom{1001}{500}$.
Sum of coefficients $= \binom{1001}{499} + \binom{1001}{500} = \binom{1002}{500}$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Set $A$ represents the closed disk $|z - 2| \le 4$ with center $C(2, 0)$ and radius $R = 4$.
Set $B$ represents the ellipse $|z - 2| + |z + 2| = 5$ with foci at $(\pm 2, 0)$ and semi-major axis $a = 2.5$.
The maximum distance between any point in $A$ and any point in $B$ occurs from the leftmost vertex of the ellipse $z_2 = -2.5$ to the point in $A$ farthest from it:
$$\max |z_1 - z_2| = |(-2.5) - 2| + R = 4.5 + 4 = 8.5 = \frac{17}{2}$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Points are $A(2, 0)$, $B(-2, 0)$, $P(2\cos\alpha, 2\sin\alpha)$, and $Q(2\sin\alpha, -2\cos\alpha)$.
Let $t = \tan(\alpha/2)$. Then:
Line $BP$: passes through $(-2, 0)$ with slope $\frac{2\sin\alpha}{2\cos\alpha+2} = t \implies y = t(x+2) \implies t = \frac{y}{x+2}$.
Line $AQ$: passes through $(2, 0)$ with slope $\frac{-2\cos\alpha}{2\sin\alpha-2} = \frac{1+t}{1-t} \implies y(1-t) = (1+t)(x-2)$.
Substituting $t = \frac{y}{x+2}$:
$$y\left(1 - \frac{y}{x+2}\right) = \left(1 + \frac{y}{x+2}\right)(x-2) \implies y(x+2-y) = (x+2+y)(x-2)$$
$$xy + 2y - y^2 = x^2 + xy - 2y - 4 \implies x^2 + y^2 - 4y - 4 = 0$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Evaluating $f(x) = \operatorname{Sgn}(\sin x) + \operatorname{Sgn}(\cos x) + \operatorname{Sgn}(\tan x) + \operatorname{Sgn}(\cot x)$ across quadrants:
- Quadrant 1: $\sin x > 0, \cos x > 0, \tan x > 0, \cot x > 0 \implies f(x) = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4$.
- Quadrant 2: $\sin x > 0, \cos x < 0, \tan x < 0, \cot x < 0 \implies f(x) = 1 - 1 - 1 - 1 = -2$.
- Quadrant 3: $\sin x < 0, \cos x < 0, \tan x > 0, \cot x > 0 \implies f(x) = -1 - 1 + 1 + 1 = 0$.
- Quadrant 4: $\sin x < 0, \cos x > 0, \tan x < 0, \cot x < 0 \implies f(x) = -1 + 1 - 1 - 1 = -2$.
The distinct values in the range are $\{-2, 0, 4\}$.
Sum of all elements in the range $= -2 + 0 + 4 = 2$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Let $\theta_1 = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\right) \implies \tan\theta_1 = \frac{2}{3}$.
$$\tan(2\theta_1) = \frac{2(2/3)}{1 - 4/9} = \frac{4/3}{5/9} = \frac{12}{5}$$
Let $\theta_2 = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right) \implies \tan\theta_2 = \frac{1}{3}$.
$$\tan(2\theta_2) = \frac{2(1/3)}{1 - 1/9} = \frac{2/3}{8/9} = \frac{3}{4}$$
Then:
$$\tan(2\theta_1 - 2\theta_2) = \frac{\tan(2\theta_1) - \tan(2\theta_2)}{1 + \tan(2\theta_1)\tan(2\theta_2)} = \frac{\frac{12}{5} - \frac{3}{4}}{1 + \frac{12}{5}\cdot\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{33/20}{56/20} = \frac{33}{56}$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Statement I:
Modulo 7 arithmetic:
$$25 \equiv -3 \implies 25^{13} \equiv -3^{13} \pmod 7$$
$$20 \equiv -1 \implies 20^{13} \equiv -1 \pmod 7$$
$$8 \equiv 1 \implies 8^{13} \equiv 1 \pmod 7$$
$$25^{13} + 20^{13} + 8^{13} + 3^{13} \equiv -3^{13} - 1 + 1 + 3^{13} \equiv 0 \pmod 7$$
Thus, it is divisible by 7. Statement I is True.

Statement II:
Let $(7 + 4\sqrt{3})^{25} = I + f$ and $f' = (7 - 4\sqrt{3})^{25}$, where $0 < f, f' < 1$.
$$I + f + f' = (7+4\sqrt{3})^{25} + (7-4\sqrt{3})^{25} = 2k \quad (\text{an even integer})$$
Since $0 < f + f' < 2$, we have $f + f' = 1$, which gives $I = 2k - 1$ (an odd integer).
Thus, the integral part is odd. Statement II is False.
Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Given $\frac{1/a + 1/b}{2} = \frac{5}{16} \implies \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{5}{8}$.
Since $a, 4, \alpha, b$ are in A.P., with common difference $d = 4 - a$:
$$\alpha = 4 + d = 8 - a, \quad b = 8 - a + d = 12 - 2a$$
Substituting $b$:
$$\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{12-2a} = \frac{5}{8} \implies \frac{12-a}{12a-2a^2} = \frac{5}{8} \implies 5a^2 - 34a + 48 = 0$$
$$(5a - 24)(a - 2) = 0$$
Since $a > 2$, $a = 4.8$. Then $\alpha = 8 - 4.8 = 3.2$ and $b = 2.4$.
Now the equation $\alpha x^2 - ax + 2(\alpha - 2b) = 0$ becomes:
$$3.2 x^2 - 4.8 x - 3.2 = 0 \implies 2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0$$
$$(2x + 1)(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = 2, \quad x = -0.5$$
The roots are $2 \in (1, 4)$ and $-0.5 \in (-2, 0)$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
Given $f(x) = 1 - 2x + \mathrm{e}^x \int_0^x \mathrm{e}^{-t} f(t)\,\mathrm{d}t$.
Differentiating with respect to $x$:
$$f'(x) = -2 + \mathrm{e}^x \int_0^x \mathrm{e}^{-t} f(t)\,\mathrm{d}t + f(x) = -2 + (f(x) - 1 + 2x) + f(x) = 2f(x) + 2x - 3$$
$$f'(x) - 2f(x) = 2x - 3$$
Solving this first-order linear ODE with $f(0) = 1$ yields $f(x) = 1 - x$.
Then $g'(x) = (f(x) + 2)^{15} (x - 4)^6 (x + 12)^{17} = -(x - 3)^{15} (x - 4)^6 (x + 12)^{17}$.
Critical points:
- At $x = 3$, $g'(x)$ changes from $+$ to $-$, so $x = 3$ is a local maximum $\implies q = 3$.
- At $x = -12$, $g'(x)$ changes from $-$ to $+$, so $x = -12$ is a local minimum $\implies p = -12$.
- At $x = 4$, the power is even, so sign does not change.
$$|p + q| = |-12 + 3| = 9$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
The lift travels from ground floor up to the 10th floor (10 floors above ground).
The lift does not stop at floors 1, 2, and 3.
Thus, the available floors to exit are floors 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (a total of 7 floors).
The number of ways in which 3 persons can exit at 3 different floors is:
$${}^7\mathrm{P}_3 = 7 \times 6 \times 5 = 210$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Let $C = A - I = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$.
$$C^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = O$$
Since $A = I + C$ and $C^2 = O$:
$$A^{100} = (I + C)^{100} = I + 100 C$$
Given $A^{100} = 100 B + I \implies B = C$.
Thus, $B^{100} = C^{100} = O$.
The sum of all elements of $B^{100}$ is $0$.

subject: Maths
explanation:
The $r$-th term can be decomposed as:
$$T_r = \frac{r}{r^4 + r^2 + 1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{r^2 - r + 1} - \frac{1}{r^2 + r + 1}\right)$$
Summing from $r = 1$ to $25$ gives a telescoping series:
$$\sum_{r=1}^{25} T_r = \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \frac{1}{25^2 + 25 + 1}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \frac{1}{651}\right) = \frac{325}{651}$$
Here $p = 325, q = 651$ with $\gcd(325, 651) = 1$.
$$p + q = 325 + 651 = 976$$

subject: Maths
explanation:
Direction unit vector along $\langle 3, -1, 0 \rangle$ is $\hat{u} = \frac{3\hat{i} - \hat{j}}{\sqrt{10}}$.
A point $Q$ at distance $13\sqrt{10}$ from $P(43, \alpha, \beta)$ along this line is:
$$Q = (43, \alpha, \beta) \pm 13(3, -1, 0) = (43 \pm 39, \alpha \mp 13, \beta)$$
Since $Q$ lies on line $\vec{r} = (4+2\mu)\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + (-1+3\mu)\hat{k}$:
- $y$-coordinate: $\alpha \mp 13 = 0 \implies \alpha = \pm 13$.
- $x$-coordinate: $4 + 2\mu = 43 \pm 39$.
For the '$-$' case: $4 + 2\mu = 4 \implies \mu = 0 \implies \beta = -1 < 0$ (satisfies condition) and $\alpha = -13$.
For the '$+$' case: $4 + 2\mu = 82 \implies \mu = 39 \implies \beta = 116 > 0$ (rejected).
Thus, $\alpha = -13, \beta = -1$.
$$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (-13)^2 + (-1)^2 = 169 + 1 = 170$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
For a prism, the refractive index is $n = \frac{\sin((A+\delta_m)/2)}{\sin(A/2)}$.
Given $\delta_m = A$:
$$n = \frac{\sin A}{\sin(A/2)} = 2\cos(A/2)$$
For light to be transmitted without total internal reflection, $A < 2\theta_c \implies \sin(A/2) < \sin\theta_c = \frac{1}{n}$.
$$n < \frac{1}{\sin(A/2)} \implies 2\cos(A/2) < \frac{1}{\sin(A/2)} \implies \sin A < 1 \implies A < 90^\circ$$
Since $0 < A < 90^\circ$, we have $0 < A/2 < 45^\circ$, which means $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} < \cos(A/2) < 1$.
Thus, $\sqrt{2} < n < 2$.

subject: Physics
explanation:
Energy of a single photon is:
$$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{663 \times 10^{-9}} = 3 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$$
Number of photons emitted per second:
$$N = \frac{P}{E} = \frac{6 \times 10^{-3}}{3 \times 10^{-19}} = 2 \times 10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1}$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
The wave propagates in the $+z$ direction $(\hat{k})$.
The relationship between fields is $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k}$.
Given $\vec{E}$ is along $+\hat{j}$, we have $\hat{j} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k} \implies \hat{B} = -\hat{i}$.
The peak magnetic field magnitude is:
$$B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c} = \frac{54}{3 \times 10^8} = 1.8 \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}$$
Thus, $\vec{B} = -1.8 \times 10^{-7}\sin(kz - \omega t)\hat{i}\text{ T}$.

subject: Physics
explanation:
For a two-body system connected by a spring of stiffness $k = 150\text{ N/m}$, the reduced mass is:
$$\mu = \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} = \frac{1 \times 0.2}{1 + 0.2} = \frac{0.2}{1.2} = \frac{1}{6}\text{ kg}$$
The angular frequency of oscillation is:
$$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{150}{1/6}} = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ rad/s}$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
Dimensional analysis:
A. Coefficient of viscosity $[\eta] = [\mathrm{M L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-1}] \implies \text{IV}$
B. Surface tension $[T] = [\mathrm{M L}^0 \mathrm{T}^{-2}] \implies \text{III}$
C. Pressure $[P] = [\mathrm{M L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}] \implies \text{I}$
D. Surface energy (Energy) $[E] = [\mathrm{M L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-2}] \implies \text{II}$
Thus, the correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

subject: Physics
explanation:
Analysis of statements:
A. Electrostatic field lines do not form closed loops because electrostatic fields are conservative. (False)
B. Electric field lines point radially outward from positive charges $(q > 0)$. (True)
C. Gauss's Law strictly relies on the inverse-square nature of Coulomb's force. (True)
D. The work done by a static electric field along any closed loop is zero. (True)
E. Coulomb's force is a central force, so angular momentum is conserved and motion is planar. (True)
Therefore, statements B, C, D, and E are correct.

Hence, the expected least count of the instrument is $0.01\text{ mm}$.

explanation:
Nuclear radius scales with mass number as $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$.
Given $\beta = 8\alpha$:
$$\frac{R_\alpha}{R_\beta} = \left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
Since $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} \implies k = 4\pi^2 \frac{m}{T^2}$, the fractional error in $k$ is:
$$\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\frac{\Delta t}{t}$$
Given $m = 10\text{ g}, \Delta m = 10\text{ mg} = 0.01\text{ g}$ and $t = 60\text{ s}, \Delta t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{\Delta k}{k} \times 100\% = \left(\frac{0.01}{10}\right) \times 100\% + 2\left(\frac{2}{60}\right) \times 100\%$$
$$= 0.1\% + 6.67\% = 6.77\% \approx 6.76\%$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
In the accelerated reference frame of the incline, the pseudo force $m a_0$ acts horizontally to the right.
Net acceleration along the incline downwards:
$$a = g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta$$
The length of the incline is $s = \frac{L}{\cos\theta}$.
Time taken to slide down:
$$t = \sqrt{\frac{2s}{a}} = \sqrt{\frac{2L}{\cos\theta(g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta)}} = \sqrt{\frac{4L}{2g\sin\theta\cos\theta - 2a_0\cos^2\theta}} = \sqrt{\frac{4L}{g\sin 2\theta - a_0(1+\cos 2\theta)}}$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
A. In series combination, $\frac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \sum \frac{1}{C_i} \implies C_{\text{eq}} < C_{\min}$. (True)
B. Dielectrics undergo bound charge displacement (polarization) under an electric field. (False)
C. $C = \frac{\varepsilon A}{d}$, so increasing $A$ or decreasing $d$ increases capacitance. (True)
D. Potential due to a point charge depends only on distance $r$, so concentric spheres are equipotential surfaces. (True)
Thus, statements A, C, and D are correct.

subject: Physics
explanation:
Initially $R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = R_4 = R$. With a supply of $40\text{ V}$:
$V_a = \frac{V}{2} = 20\text{ V}$.
After heating, $R_3 = 1.1 R$:
$$V_b = V \frac{R_4}{R_3 + R_4} = 40 \left(\frac{R}{1.1R + R}\right) = \frac{40}{2.1} \approx 19.05\text{ V}$$
$$V_a - V_b = 20 - 19.05 = 0.95\text{ V}$$

subject: Physics
explanation: Absolute electric potential (voltage at a single point) is defined with respect to an arbitrary reference and cannot be directly measured physically. Only potential difference (voltage difference) between two points is physically measurable.

subject: Physics
explanation:
Speed of longitudinal wave is $v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$.
$$\frac{\Delta v}{v} \approx \frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta Y}{Y} - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} = \frac{1}{2}(1\%) - \frac{1}{2}(0.5\%) = +0.25\%$$
$$\Delta v = 400 \times \frac{0.25}{100} = +1\text{ m/s}$$
New speed $= 400 + 1 = 401\text{ m/s}$.

subject: Physics

At the central axis $(r = 0)$, the magnetic field is zero, which is the minimum value across the cross section.

subject: Physics

subject: Physics
explanation:

2. Turning point occurs when $v(t) = 12t^2 - 3 = 0 \implies t = 0.5\text{ s}$.
   At $t = 0.5$, $x(0.5) = 4(1/8) - 3(1/2) = -1$, which is at distance $1\text{ unit}$ from origin. (Statement B is True)

subject: Physics
explanation:
Mean free path is given by:
$$\lambda = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P}$$
With $T = 41 + 273 = 314\text{ K}$, $d = 5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$, $P = 1.38 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$, and $k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}$:
$$\lambda = \frac{1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times 314}{\sqrt{2} \times 3.14 \times (25 \times 10^{-20}) \times (1.38 \times 10^5)} = \frac{100 \times 10^{-23}}{25\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-15}} = 2\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}$$

subject: Physics
explanation:
Moment of inertia of flywheel is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{1}{2}(3)(25) = 37.5\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$.
Total potential energy lost as mass descends $h = 3\text{ m}$ is:
$$mgh = 3 \times 10 \times 3 = 90\text{ J}$$
By energy conservation, $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}(3)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}(3)v^2\right) = \frac{9}{4}v^2 = 90\text{ J} \implies v^2 = 40\text{ m}^2/\text{s}^2$.
Kinetic energy of the wheel:
$$K_{\text{wheel}} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{3}{4}v^2 = \frac{3}{4}(40) = 30\text{ J}$$

explanation:
In the borax bead test:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{NaBO}_2 (\text{X}) + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 (\text{Y})$$
$$\text{CuSO}_4 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Non-Luminous flame}} \text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2 (\text{Z}) + \text{SO}_3$$
In $\text{Z} = \text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2$ (cupric metaborate), $\text{Cu}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state.
$$2\text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2 + 2\text{NaBO}_2 + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\text{Luminous flame}} 2\text{CuBO}_2 (\text{Q}) + \text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 + \text{CO}$$
In $\text{Q} = \text{CuBO}_2$ (cuprous metaborate), $\text{Cu}$ is in $+1$ oxidation state.
Thus, the oxidation states of $\text{Cu}$ in $\text{Z}$ and $\text{Q}$ are $+2$ and $+1$ respectively.

explanation:
For the electrolytic buffer formed by mixing $x\text{ mL}$ of $5\text{M NaHCO}_3$ and $10\text{ mL}$ of $2\text{M H}_2\text{CO}_3$:
$$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_a + \log\left(\frac{5x}{20}\right) = 6.11 + \log\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$$
For the electrochemical cell:
$$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = -0.44 - (-0.90) = 0.46\text{ V}$$
$$E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.059}{6}\log\left(\frac{10^3}{[\text{OH}^-]^3}\right) = 0.46 - 0.0295(1 + \text{pOH})$$
Given $E_{\text{cell}} = 0.2353\text{ V}$:
$$0.0295(1 + \text{pOH}) = 0.2247 \implies 1 + \text{pOH} = 7.617 \implies \text{pH} = 7.40$$
$$6.11 + \log(x/4) = 7.40 \implies \log(x/4) = 1.29 \implies \frac{x}{4} = 19.5 \implies x = 78\text{ mL}$$
